subject: POC architecture review & vendor exit scheduling
messages:
From: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-ai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tara Brown <tara.brown@finserv.com>
Date: 2027-04-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: POC architecture review & migration timeline

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this — we’re planning a short POC to evaluate moving away from our current inference provider (CloudServe AI) to a dedicated Redwood deployment. Key drivers: consistent latency, lower per-token cost at scale, and better fallback policies for peak trading hours.

We’d like a technical deep-dive to validate mapping our current setup (self-hosted adapters + CloudServe managed endpoints) to Redwood’s Dedicated offering. Ideal outcomes:
- Confirm compatibility for our 4B/8B model mix and quantized runtimes
- Network/VPC requirements for FinServ compliance
- Rough timeline for a lift-and-shift PoC (2–4 weeks target)

Can you propose 2x 60-min slots next week (Apr 5–7) that include an architecture review + follow-up working session? I’ll invite our infra lead and security reviewer.

Attached: sample CloudServe topology (see referenced diagram below).

Thanks,
Rajiv
Infrastructure Lead, Acme AI
[Attachment: cloudserve-topology.pdf (PDF, 820KB)]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Tara Brown <tara.brown@finserv.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: POC architecture review & migration timeline

Rajiv — thanks for the context. This is right in our wheelhouse.

Proposed next steps:
1) 60-min architecture deep-dive (network, model compatibility, deployment patterns)
2) 90-min hands-on working session (slotting, KV cache strategy, performance targets)

I can host the deep-dive on either Tue Apr 5 at 09:00 PT or Wed Apr 6 at 14:00 PT. If one of those works for your team, I’ll send an invite and include the working session option.

Looping in Dev (solutions engineer) and Rachel (account lead) — Dev will run the tech demo and Rachel will coordinate contractual follow-ups. I attached a lightweight PoC deployment plan we typically use so your infra/security folks can skim prior to the call.

Please confirm attendee list and preferred slot.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: poc-deployment-plan.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

From: Tara Brown <tara.brown@finserv.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: POC architecture review & migration timeline

Thanks Neha. Either option could work for us but preference is Tue Apr 5 at 09:00 PT — earlier the better so we can discuss networking before end of week.

Attendees from FinServ: Tara Brown (infra/product), Leo Chang (security), Priya Menon (platform). Leo will join for the network/VPC section only.

I’m also including Markus from Redwood — he’ll want to confirm minimum host/network requirements and any HSM/KMS notes for our compliance team.

Attached: current network diagram (internal).

Tara
VP Platform, FinServ Corp
[Attachment: network-diagram.png (PNG, 450KB)]

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Brown <tara.brown@finserv.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-02T14:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: POC architecture review & migration timeline

Great — Tue Apr 5 at 09:00 PT is reserved on my calendar. Quick agenda proposal (60 min):
- 00–10min: Intros & current state (FinServ/Acme topology)
- 10–30min: Redwood serving runtime & Dedicated topology mapping (kernels, batching, KV cache)
- 30–45min: Network/VPC, KMS/HSM, audit logs (compliance pre-reqs)
- 45–60min: Next steps & working session scheduling

Pre-reqs for a productive session (please share ahead of time):
- Typical peak qps and 95p latency targets for production windows
- Current model sizes and whether models are quantized (4B/8B + int8?)
- Any regional restrictions / data residency notes

I’ll create the calendar invite with a Redwood-hosted Zoom link and include the PoC plan + network diagram. If anyone needs an on-prem demo environment instead of Zoom (for air-gapped review), flag it here.

—Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Brown <tara.brown@finserv.com>, Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@acme-ai.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03T15:28:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Request: POC architecture review & migration timeline

Thanks all — confirmed. Meeting created:
When: Tue, Apr 5, 2027 · 09:00–10:00 PT
Where: Zoom (Redwood) — https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=abc123
Agenda: same as Dev’s outline; we’ll follow with a 90-min hands-on slot (proposal Wed Apr 6 14:00 PT) if the deep-dive looks good.

Attachments included on invite: poc-deployment-plan.pdf, network-diagram.png
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/7890

Action items before the call:
- FinServ: share peak qps and model quantization status (Leo, Priya — can you drop those here?)
- Acme: confirm whether any proprietary runtime hooks are required for your adapters
- Redwood: Dev/Markus to prepare a brief matrix of recommended instance types and a rough cost delta for Dedicated vs hosted for your expected volume

If you need to reschedule, please reply to this thread and Rachel will propose alternates. Looking forward to it.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0198
[Attachment: invite.ics]
